mia-sales: quick sync — ACME wants a 4-week POC. Need a compact internal runbook + an external checklist sales can paste. Focus: hosted API keys, dedicated pool, private/VPC. Who owns each step and rough timelines?

chloe-ps: External checklist (one-paragraph + bullets we can copy):
- One-liner: "Choose Hosted for fastest demo (same-day API key), Dedicated for predictable latency / SLA (2-3 days), Private/VPC for compliance or data residency (1-2+ weeks)."
- Required from customer: access type, target QPS, avg sequence length, sample prompt, data sensitivity level, preferred region, networking contact (VPC owner), and SSO admin email.
- Deliverables from us: API key (hosted) or pool reservation (dedicated) or infra template + install window (private).

alex-ml: sizing heuristics we should include to help sales estimate:
- Light demo: <10 rps, avg seq 64 tokens -> hosted fine
- Perf trial: 50-200 rps or bursty -> dedicated, recommend L40/A10G depending on latency target
- High-throughput embeddings (batch) -> dedicated with batching config
- Guidance sample: "For 100 rps and 256 avg tokens, plan for 4 L40 slots with batching and 500ms target p95."

sam-eng: Internal provisioning runbook (concise, step-by-step). Keep names consistent (redwood-<dealid>-poc).
1) Hosted (fast path, same-day)
  - Owner: eng-platform
  - Steps:
    - Create tenant tag: redwood:deal=ACME-146
    - Create API key (POC TTL 30d + tag poc=true)
      ```bash
      redwood keys create --tenant ACME-146 --tags "poc=true,deal=ACME-146" --ttl 30d
      ```
    - Apply soft quota (default 500k tokens/day) and enable streaming
      ```json
      { "quota_tokens_per_day": 500000, "features": ["streaming","function_calling"] }
      ```
    - Add billing note: deal=ACME-146
  - Timeline: same business day if requested before 4pm PT
2) Dedicated (predictable perf)
  - Owner: infra + eng-platform
  - Pre-reqs: signed SOW / commit, GPU type (A10G/L40), desired slots
  - Steps:
    - Reserve pool: record pool_id and tag with deal
      ```text
      infra reserve-pool --type L40 --slots 4 --tag deal=ACME-146
      ```
    - Set autoscale policy: min=1 max=3 (adjust after trial)
    - Create service account: redwood-ACME-146-svc (SSH key if admin access)
    - Route customer model endpoint -> dedicated pool with fallback to hosted
    - Run canary job on non-prod before attach
  - Timeline: typical 48-72 hours after SOW
3) Private / VPC (compliance path)
  - Owner: eng-infra + security + it-oncall
  - Pre-reqs from customer: VPC CIDR, peering info, firewall owner, KMS ARN, SCIM/SAML contact
  - Steps:
    - Send infra template (see snippet below)
      ```yaml
      vpc_cidr: 10.20.0.0/16
      required_subnets: [10.20.1.0/24, 10.20.2.0/24]
      peering: accept
      outbound_hosts: [logging, s3]
      ```
    - Validate IAM/KMS access and S3 access for model bits/logs
    - Schedule 2-3 hour install window with oncall and infra leads
    - Post-install: enable audit logs -> forward to customer SIEM, verify KMS key rotation policy
  - Timeline: 1-2+ weeks depending on procurement & network approvals

nina-security: Security gating checklist to block or approve installs — all required before private install:
- Completed security questionnaire (signed) + SOC2 checklist
- Network flow diagram with egress rules and firewall ACL owner
- KMS key ARN and rotation policy; IAM role that our install will assume
- SCIM endpoint + SSO admin for SSO provisioning
- SLA for log retention and access control list (who can read logs)
- Expected timeline note: security sign-off usually 3-7 business days

infra-bot: automation tips / quick commands we use internally:
- Reserve pool (CLI): infra-cli pool reserve --project ACME-146 --gpu L40 --count 4 --tags poc=true
- Create ephemeral service account: infra-cli svc create --name redwood-ACME-146-svc --scopes "read,deploy"
- Quota apply: infra-cli quota set --tenant ACME-146 --tokens 500000

chloe-ps: Naming & lifecycle policy (to avoid cleanup debt):
- Resources use prefix: redwood-<dealid>-poc (examples: redwood-ACME-146-pool1, redwood-ACME-146-key)
- API keys auto-expire in 30 days; ops will send reminder 7d before expiry
- All POC service accounts created with minimal scopes; escalate for admin access only after approval

it-oncall: preferred install windows (UTC-7): Tue 09:00-11:00, Wed 14:00-17:00. Need firewall contact and one VPN rope-in. Please include oncall pager and escalation lead in invite.

deploy-bot: automation note: poc-key-ttl enforcer v2.0 deployed to staging 2025-11-02T03:21:00Z — will tag keys and set TTL automatically.

mia-sales: blockers to call out so sales can set expectations:
- Missing VPC peering details or firewall owner
- Procurement delays for SOW (Dedicated)
- KMS approvals (security/legal) for private installations
- High unanticipated QPS requiring pool resize

chloe-ps: final internal runbook summary (one-paragraph for handbook):
"Use Hosted for same-day demos (create API key, soft quota, streaming), Dedicated when predictable latency or throughput is required (reserve GPU pool, service account, autoscale), and Private when compliance or data residency is mandatory (collect VPC/KMS/SSO docs, schedule install, enable audit logs). Follow resource naming and TTL policies, attach deal ID to billing notes, and route to infra/security owners for approvals."
